title: Trim CI runtime images and deploy hybrid content-addressable + local warm cache
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Our monolithic CI builder images and cold-only remote cache have increased pipeline runtime and flakiness. Common changes (lint, unit tests, small Go/Python/Node deps) still trigger full image unpack or remote cache misses, resulting in median CI time ~18m for incremental PRs and frequent timeout flakes on cold runners.

Goal: Reduce end-to-end median incremental CI runtime to <8m for typical PRs, cut bandwidth by 40% from cold pulls, and reduce flaky failures caused by cache misses and transient network issues. Achieve this by: 1) splitting the giant builder into curated runtime shards (language/tool-specific minimal images), 2) deploying a hybrid artifact cache that combines existing CAS (s3-backed) with a small warm local LRU cache on runners, and 3) upgrading and pinning lint/toolchains with caching hooks.

Why now: Ongoing platform scalability issues are impacting dev velocity and build cost. Several recent infra incidents traced to large image pulls during autoscaling. This is a medium-sized tech-debt initiative with high impact on daily developer experience.
acceptance_criteria: Median incremental PR CI time reduced from 18m to <=8m for 80% of PRs in the main monorepo over a 2-week window
Cold-runner image pull bandwidth reduced by >=40% measured across 7-day aggregate
Flake rate due to cache misses or image fetch timeouts reduced by >=60% compared to baseline
Hybrid cache deployed to CI fleet (rollout flags) with metrics and dashboarding visible in the CI observability board
New minimal images published to internal registry with SBOM and size tags; secure scan passes
Toolchain upgrades for Node 20, Python 3.11, and Go 1.21 completed and locked in builder manifests with backward-compatible fallbacks
implementation_notes: Phase 1 (spike, 2w): analyze most common CI job archetypes, produce image-shard matrix and identify top-6 size offenders

Phase 2 (image refactor, 3w): create minimal runtime images: node-runtime, python-runtime, go-runtime, base-compile, lint-shim. Each image <700MB when gzipped and includes SBOM and security-scan step.
Phase 3 (cache infra, 2w): implement local LRU warm cache daemon on runners (~4GB footprint), integrate with existing CAS (S3), implement two-layer lookup: local -> CAS -> remote-origin
Phase 4 (toolchain pinning + hooks, 1w): add toolchain cache hooks for pip wheels, npm ci cache, and go module proxy; include checksum validation and telemetry
Phase 5 (rollout, 2w): feature-flag rollout to 10%/50%/100% of runners with automated rollback on error budget triggers, update dashboards, and deprecate old monolithic image by tag
Non-goals: full rewrite of CI orchestration or changing executor provider; not addressing long-running integration job optimization in this ticket
progress_updates: 2025-11-12: Spike completed. Identified that 62% of CI time in incremental runs comes from image unpack + dependency fetch. Proposed image shard matrix attached.
2025-11-28: Built prototype node-runtime and python-runtime images; node image reduced from 1.9GB -> 420MB gzipped in test environment. Uploaded SBOM to internal artifact store.
2025-12-08: Hybrid cache design reviewed with infra and security. Decided to limit local warm cache to 4GB per runner and encrypt cache on disk. Security requested an HLD doc (confluence link below).

2026-01-18: Toolchain upgrade validation: Node 20 passed CI test matrix with 1 minor flaky test in auth-service; tracked as ENG-94111. Python 3.11 tests passing across services after pinning numpy wheels.
2026-02-25: Canary rollout (10%) of hybrid cache started. Early results: canary median incremental run = 7.6m vs baseline 18m; cold-run bandwidth on canary runners down 48%.
2026-03-06: 50% rollout completed. Observability dashboard added: ci/runner/cache_hit_ratio and ci/runner/image_pull_duration. No increase in error budget so far.
2026-03-10: PRs opened for image manifests and runner daemon: GH-ops/ci-runner#238 and GH-infra/ci-cache#451. Requesting PM & Security review before full fleet rollout.
blockers: Security review required for local cache encryption and SBOM handling (security requested extended threat model analysis)
Runner agent upgrade dependency: fleet majority still on agent v1.12 which lacks ephemeral cache API; rollout requires coordinated agent bump
Storage cost analysis for increasing ephemeral disk allocation per runner pending finance approval
review_feedback: PM (Priya Rao) 2026-02-28: Strong 👍 on developer velocity metrics. Ask: include migration notes for on-call and runbook updates.
Security (Noah Bennett) 2026-03-02: Require encryption-at-rest for local cache and SBOM retention policy; asked to add periodic cache purge logic tied to runner lifecycle.
Infra (Marcus Li) 2026-03-04: Suggest making local cache optional per pool to control disk pressure; flagged agent upgrade coordination as gating.
QA (Lina Fernández) 2026-03-05: Request end-to-end resiliency tests simulating CAS outage and local cache corruption; proposed test harness in GH-actions
follow_ups: ENG-94111: fix minor auth-service flaky test found during Node 20 validation
ENG-94902: runner agent upgrade and ephemeral-disk migration (dependent)
PM-412: update developer docs, runbook, and postmortem template for cache incidents
